overview.mechanism: A water-soluble vitamin; degradation of ascorbate can generate oxalate.
uses: Prevention or treatment of vitamin C deficiency using the appropriate formulation; oral supplements and intravenous injection have different labeling.

paragraphs.text: A 2026 scoping review of oral and intravenous vitamin C case reports identified pre-existing renal dysfunction as a risk factor for impaired clearance during large-dose exposure. Case reports have important confounding and cannot establish a universal safe threshold.

The US intravenous ASCOR label warns about oxalate nephropathy and nephrolithiasis and provides route-specific administration precautions. Its intravenous regimen must not be applied to oral tablets or syrup.

sources.citation: Carr and Gupta. Are oral and intravenous vitamin C implicated in oxalate-associated renal failure? Exploring pre-existing renal dysfunction. Nutr Res. 2026;155:148–163. PubMed PMID: 42925834.
ASCOR (ascorbic acid injection) US prescribing information. DailyMed. Reference product; Philippine labeling may differ.

revision_log.change: Source-linked descriptive overview and clinical evidence; no new unsupported dose recommendation or inferred dialysis schedule.
